name: Somalia
summary: A white five-pointed star on a light blue field. The star's five points represent the five regions where Somali people live, reflecting the ideal of a Greater Somalia.
origin: Mohammed Awale Liban designed the flag for the UN Trust Territory of Somaliland under Italian administration; it was adopted on 12 October 1954.
When British Somaliland and the Trust Territory united on 1 July 1960 to form the Somali Republic, the flag became the national flag.

colors.name: Light blue
colors.meaning: Originally in honour of the United Nations, which administered the territory; also the sky and the Indian Ocean.

symbols.name: Star of Unity
symbols.description: A white five-pointed star in the centre.
symbols.meaning: The five regions inhabited by Somalis: former British Somaliland, former Italian Somaliland, Djibouti, the Ogaden (Ethiopia) and the North Eastern Province (Kenya).

facts: Its blue was chosen in tribute to the UN flag.
Somaliland, a self-declared state in the north, uses a separate flag of green, white and red with the Shahada.
The Federated States of Micronesia's flag is also light blue with white stars.
clues: A white star on a light blue field.
Its star's points stand for five regions where one people live.
Its blue honours the United Nations.
